---
title: "check-citation-authors.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags an author's surname
typed next to a citation of the same source.
An in-text citation, `@key`, already prints the author names,
so the sentence around it should not type them again
(psw's [Let the citation name the source](https://morrison-lab.github.io/psw/chapters/citations-evidence.html#let-citation-name-source),
[#2144](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/2144)).

Flagged:

```markdown
The figure follows the layout of a figure in James et al.
[@james2021islr, Figure 6.7].
```

Preferred:

```markdown
The figure follows the layout of @james2021islr [Figure 6.7].
```

## What it flags

In `.qmd` and `.md` files,
a capitalized word within six words before a citation key,
when the key starts with that word in lower case,
as `James` and `@james2021islr` do.
The key can sit in brackets (`[@key]`, `[see @key, p. 3]`),
in parentheses (`(@key)`), or stand bare.
The match leans on the lab's bib keys,
which start with the first author's surname.

The comparison folds case and accents,
drops a possessive `'s`,
and joins a lowercase particle to the name after it,
so `van Buuren` matches `@vanbuuren2018`
and `Bienaymé` matches `@bienayme1853`.

The six words may reach back onto the previous line of the same paragraph,
since the notes break lines at clauses,
and they stop at the end of the previous sentence.
`et al.` and an initial such as `J.` do not end a sentence.

## What it does not flag

- an author-suppressed citation, `[-@key]`,
  where the typed name is the only one printed;
- a crossref such as `@fig-x` or `@sec-y`, and an email address;
- a name inside link text or emphasis,
  where it is part of a term or a title,
  as in `[Cook's distance](#def-cooks)` or `**Cox proportional hazards**`;
- a one-letter word, or a word that is not capitalized;
- code fences and code spans, HTML comments, and YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following,
  `<!-- check-citation-authors: allow: <reason> -->`.
  The reason is required,
  for example a sentence that names one author of a multi-author source on purpose.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing pages never block.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

The check is warn-only by default
while its false-positive rate is measured.
A whole-tree run on 2026-11-20 found 2 hits in psw, 2 in rme, and 190 in lds,
nearly all of them true.
The false ones were a standard named by its number
and an eponym written outside emphasis.

## Limitations

- An eponym written as plain text, such as `the Elman recurrent layer [@elman1990time]`,
  is flagged; mark it with the allow comment or put the term in bold.
- A bib key that does not start with the first author's surname is never matched.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `false` | Fail the workflow when a typed author name is found. Warn-only by default while the false-positive rate is measured. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository, because [a public repository's pull requests can run arbitrary code on it](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-citation-authors.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a line a PR adds that types an author's surname next to
# a citation of the same source, such as "James et al. [@james2021islr, Figure 6.7]",
# where "@james2021islr [Figure 6.7]" already prints the names.
# Warn-only by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check citation authors

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-citation-authors.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                              # fail on a finding (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-citation-authors.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-citation-authors.yml)
for the full caller stub.
